ruling.recommended_action: Close the route-deviation complaint with no refund; the metered fare of $29.26 stands, no account action on either party.
ruling.reasoning:
The complaint is that the driver left the app's route and the meter exceeded the estimate [F1][F2]. The trip is RydeTAXI, so the fare is metered and extra kilometres do enter the fare directly; the remedy therefore turns on RD-2 read with RD-1 [RD-1][RD-2]. The fare breakdown itself is clean: base $3.90 + distance $17.48 (12.40 km) + time $6.41 (24.7 min) + platform $1.47 = $29.26, waiting $0.00, and surge 1.0× so no undisclosed add-on arises [F5][F6]; nothing is refundable under FARE-1 [FARE-1].

RD-1 identifies exactly one off-route segment: 09:03–09:11, 3.97 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.80 km, adding 2.18 km and reaching up to 1040 m off route [F1][F3]. That segment is exempt or not under RD-4(a) and RD-4(b) [RD-4]. The trace settles the (a) element: the DataMall accident report (Tampines Expressway towards PIE after Punggol Road Exit, "avoid lane 1") was reported at 08:44, 0 m from the optimal route, and falls within 300 m of the replaced stretch [F12]. Under RD-4(a) that report is an incident on the replaced portion of optimal route, logged before the segment began and still listed in the trip window, which exempts the segment; the band-1 record on the same road (0–9 km/h, 08:47–09:03) is corroboration only and cannot by itself exempt under RD-4(b) [F9][F10][F11]. The driver's post-trip statement that lanes were blocked and the diversion unavoidable [F8] is not needed for the exemption and would not, on its own, establish it.

There is no consent question to decide: the chat record contains no in-app messages at all, so no rider message exists before the segment start at 09:03 [F7], and the driver makes no RD-5 claim [F8][RD-5]. Because the single segment is exempt, there is no unexempted extra_km and no refundable base [F3][RD-2]. The residual 0.38 km (billed excess 2.56 km at $3.61 minus the segment's 2.18 km) is route-corridor / map-matching mileage that RD-2 expressly does not refund; it yields $0.00 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The refund formula in the trace therefore produces Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments × $1.4097/km = 0 km × $1.4097/km = $0.00, so the outcome is no_action; the driver's RD-1 obligation still has to be read against the exemption, and no account flag follows [RD-6].

SAFE-1 screening: I read the rider's complaint, the chat record and the driver's statement; none contains a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8][RD-1][RD-2]. The evidence record is complete for what this ruling needs — GPS segment measurement, fare breakdown and incident record are all present [F3][F6][F12] — so no gap remains.

The rider's own concession that RD-4(a) exempts the replaced stretch is accepted in full: the accident report sits 0 m from the optimal route and within the replaced stretch of the single segment [F12][F3][RD-4].

The 09:03 end of the band-1 window [F9] does not limit the RD-4(a) exemption, which rests on the incident report [F12] rather than on band evidence; RD-4(b) is corroboration only, so F9–F11 neither exempt nor unexempt anything by themselves [RD-4].

The metered fare breakdown [F6] and the billed excess of $3.61 on 2.56 km [F4] do not create a refund base once the only extra_km-bearing segment is exempt: RD-2 refunds only unexempted segments' extra_km, which is zero here [F3][RD-2].

No fact partitions the 2.18 km of the single segment [F3] into an incident-covered part and a non-covered part; a segment exempt under RD-4(a) cannot be split without a per-metre traffic match the record does not supply, so the claimed $3.07 rests on no measured extra_km [F3][F12][RD-2][RD-4].

Accepted as far as it goes — the rider's unupheld dispute history [F14] and the driver's 0 upheld disputes [F15] mean RD-6's precondition is unmet [RD-6] — but this profile facts cannot establish the deviation itself, and the deviation is exempt on the incident record [F12][RD-4][RD-6].

Accepted in outcome (no refund) but the driver's description of the residual as 'route corridor / map-matching residual [F3][F1]' is not what RD-2 turns on here: the refund is zero because the sole segment is exempt, not because the residual is unclassified [RD-2][RD-4].

The $0.54 cap on the 0.38 km outside the segment [F3][F4] is not a refundable amount: RD-2 refunds extra_km of unexempted segments only, and corridor / map-matching mileage is expressly not refunded, so the arithmetic yields $0.00 [RD-2].

Accepted: the $29.26 breakdown [F6] with surge 1.0× [F5] contains no unpublished add-on, so FARE-1 strips nothing — but this only confirms there is no fare-detail refund, not the exemption [FARE-1][RD-2].
Accepted: 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F15] fails RD-6's precondition, so no flag_account attaches to this ruling [RD-6].
